title: OTWONO Egress Source
description: One place this node is permitted to fetch from. Sources live in /etc/otwono/fetch.d/*.toml and are the whole of what otwono-fetchd will contact: a caller names a source and a path suffix under its prefix, never a URL, so the host, scheme, port and query string are the operator's decision rather than the caller's. Adding a source is a policy.write and confirms; see ADR-0014. This document describes the TOML file as parsed, expressed as JSON.

source.description: Zero or more sources. An empty or absent list permits nothing, which is the shipped default.

id.description: Stable name a caller uses in fetch.get, and the resource a net.fetch capability token is bound to — so policy can grant one source and not another.

host.description: Fully qualified DNS name, lowercase. Never an IP literal (the `not` clause refuses a dotted-quad): the allow-list exists to be read by a person deciding whether to approve it, and a name is also what TLS verifies against. Lowercase is required so the file reads the way the code compares it — matching itself is case-insensitive.

port.description: Omit for 443. The scheme is always https and is deliberately not configurable, so no file can turn a source into cleartext.

path_prefix.description: Absolute, slash-terminated. Every request is composed as this prefix followed by the caller's suffix. The trailing slash is required: without it a suffix could extend the last segment, so a prefix of /otwono/model would also reach /otwono/models-elsewhere.

max_bytes.description: Hard cap on one object fetched from this source. Checked against the size the server states before any transfer begins, and again as bytes arrive.
